papers.title: Sharp Fractional Capacitary-Distance Hardy Inequalities
papers.abstract: Let $d\in\mathbb N$, $p\in(1,\infty)$, $p':=\frac{p}{p-1}$, and $s\in(0,\min\{1+\frac1p,\frac dp\})$. For an open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, let $F:=\mathbb{R}^d\setminus\Omega$. For any $\alpha\in(0,1]$ and $x\in\Omega$, let \begin{align*} d_{\alpha,s,p}(x) :=\inf\left\{r\in(0,\infty): \frac{\operatorname{cap}_{s,p}(\overline{F\cap B(x,r)})} {\operatorname{cap}_{s,p}(\overline{B(x,r)})}\ge\alpha\right\}, \end{align*} where $\operatorname{cap}_{s,p}$ is the capacity associated with the fractional Sobolev energy $[\,\cdot\,]_{s,p}^p$. In this article, we prove that there exists a positive constant $C$, depending only on $d$, $s$, and $p$, such that, for any $\alpha\in(0,1]$ and $u\in C_{\rm c}^\infty(\Omega)$, \begin{align*} \int_\Omega\frac{|u(x)|^p}{d_{\alpha,s,p}(x)^{sp}}\,dx \le C\alpha^{-p'}[u]_{s,p}^p. \end{align*} We also show that both the exponent $p'$ in $\alpha^{-p'}$ as $\alpha\to0^+$ over the class of all open sets and the range $s\in(0,1+\frac1p)$ within $sp<d$ are sharp. Our proofs use variational minimization, equilibrium measures on trees, and weighted Hardy inequalities.

papers.title: Sharp Weak-Type Inequalities for Scalar and Matrix Weights
papers.abstract: Let $p\in(1,\infty)$ and $p':=\frac p{p-1}$. In this article, we establish a mixed multiplier weak-type inequality with weight dependence $[w]_{A_p}^{\frac1p}[w]_{A_\infty}^{\max\{\frac1p,\frac1{p'}\}}$ for scalar $A_p$ weights and Calder\'on--Zygmund operators whose modulus of continuity satisfies the Dini condition. As a consequence, we obtain the sharp exponent $\max\{1,\frac2p\}$ of $[w]_{A_p}$ in the corresponding pure $A_p$ bound. Moreover, in the matrix-weighted setting, we prove the sharpness of the exponent $1+\min\{\frac1p,\frac1{p(p-1)}\}$ of $[W]_{\mathcal A_p}$ in the known multiplier weak-type inequality for the Hilbert transform.

papers.title: Almost minimizing Yang$-$Mills fields: log-epiperimetric inequality, non-concentration, and uniqueness of tangents
papers.abstract: We establish a direct log-epiperimetric inequality for Yang$-$Mills fields in arbitrary dimension and we leverage it to prove uniqueness of tangent cones with isolated singularity for almost energy minimizing connections and $\omega$-ASD connections (where $\omega$ is not necessarily closed) satisfying some suitable regularity and non-concentration assumptions. En route to this we establish a Luckhaus type lemma for connections to exclude curvature concentration along blow-up sequences.

papers.title: Fine properties of nonlinear potentials and a unified perspective on monotonicity formulas
papers.abstract: We rigorously show that a large family of monotone quantities along the weak inverse mean curvature flow is the limit case of the corresponding ones along the level sets of $p$-capacitary potentials. Such monotone quantities include Willmore and Minkowski-type functionals on Riemannian manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature. In $3$-dimensional manifolds with nonnegative scalar curvature, we also recover the monotonicity of the Hawking mass and its nonlinear potential theoretic counterparts. This unified view is built on a refined analysis of $p$-capacitary potentials. We prove that they strongly converge in $W^{1,q}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ as $p\to 1^+$ to the inverse mean curvature flow and their level sets are curvature varifolds. Finally, we also deduce a Gauss-Bonnet-type theorem for level sets of $p$-capacitary potentials.

papers.title: Banach-Mazur distance and related methods of comparing convex bodies
papers.abstract: The Banach-Mazur distance is one of the standard tools used in the study of mathematical objects such as convex bodies or normed spaces, and it becomes indispensable when investigating properties that are invariant under linear isomorphisms. It appears in convex geometry and convex analysis as a way to quantify the approximation of convex bodies. In functional analysis, it plays a basic role in the study of local properties of Banach spaces. The goal of this survey is to present a cohesive picture of these two perspectives. We supply an extensive collection of known results for reference and list open problems of varying difficulty, which could stimulate further research. We include in our discussion several distinct variations on the concept of the Banach-Mazur distance, some of them exploratory, that haven't received much attention to date in the literature. We follow the trend - which emerged in recent decades - of considering arbitrary convex bodies, and not just those that are centrally symmetric. Finally, we include a comprehensive list of references on the Banach-Mazur distance.

papers.title: A counterexample to the one-supremum conjecture and sharp logarithmic weighted bounds for Calder\'on--Zygmund operators
papers.abstract: We give a negative answer to the one-supremum conjecture of Hyt\"onen and Lacey~\cite[Remark~1.3]{HL}, in the strong-type form stated by Lerner and Moen~\cite[Conjecture~1.3, formula~(9)]{LM}. The conjecture asks whether the mixed $A_p$--$A_\infty$ characteristics $K_p(w)$ and $K_{p'}(\sigma)$, with both factors evaluated on the same cube, control Calder\'on--Zygmund operators without a logarithmic loss. For every $1<p<\infty$, we construct explicit weights for which $K_p(w)+K_{p'}(\sigma)\eqsim_p m$, but one fixed Hilbert transform has weighted norm at least $m(1+\log m)^{\gamma_p}$, where $\gamma_p=\max\{1/p,1/p'\}$. Thus the proposed bound fails even for a fixed singular integral. The counterexample also extends to a fixed Riesz transform in each dimension $n\ge2$. We further establish a logarithmically corrected bound for Calder\'on--Zygmund operators, with powers $1/p'$ and $1/p$ on the respective one-supremum terms. Together, the lower and upper bounds identify $\gamma_p$ as the optimal common logarithmic exponent and give the sharp worst-case growth $(1+\log A)^{\gamma_p}$ under the constraint $[w]_{A_p}\le A$. The results show why information from any one cube cannot fully capture the accumulation of a singular integral across many scales.

papers.title: Boundedness of a Schur multiplier on the Schatten p-class, $1 < p \neq 2 < \infty$, does not imply complete boundedness
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of a bounded Schur multiplier on the Schatten class $S_p(\ell_2)$ which is not completely bounded when $1<p\ne 2<\infty$, which confirms Pisier's conjecture (1998).

papers.title: Approximation numbers of Hankel Operators on Weighted Fock Spaces and the Berger--Coburn Phenomenon
papers.abstract: Let $\varphi\in C^2(\mathbb{C}^n)$ be a real-valued weight whose real Hessian is uniformly positive definite and bounded. For $0<p<\infty$, $1\le q<\infty$, and possibly unbounded symbols $f$, we give necessary and sufficient conditions for prescribed decay of the approximation numbers of Hankel operators $H_f$ from weighted Fock spaces $F^p(\varphi)$ to weighted Lebesgue spaces $L^q(\varphi)$ in terms of the non-increasing rearrangement of the IDA function of $f$. We also characterize membership in the approximation ideals $\mathfrak A_s(F^p(\varphi),L^q(\varphi))$ and their weak counterparts $\mathfrak A_{s,\infty}(F^p(\varphi),L^q(\varphi))$ for $0<s<\infty$. The symbol criteria involve Lorentz, Lorentz--Zygmund, and Copson--Lorentz spaces. Our approach also yields the converse to the sufficient condition in [15], thereby completing the characterization of prescribed singular value decay for Hankel operators on a broad class of weighted Bergman spaces. For the pair $H_f$ and $H_{\bar f}$ on weighted Fock spaces, we characterize simultaneous decay of their approximation numbers and simultaneous membership in these ideals in terms of the mean oscillation function of $f$. For bounded symbols, we establish the Berger--Coburn phenomenon for both ideals in sharp exponent ranges. A new feature in the case $p<2<q$ is that the Berger--Coburn equivalence holds for $s_0(p,q)<s\le1$, where the sharp threshold $s_0(p,q)$ is strictly less than $1$.

papers.title: Bourin's Crossed-Heinz Inequality in the Frobenius Norm
papers.abstract: For positive semidefinite matrices $A,B \in M_n(\mathbb{C})$ and $0<t<1$, we establish the sharp quantitative Frobenius-norm inequality $\|A^t B^{1-t}+B^t A^{1-t}\|_{\mathrm{F}}^2+4t(1-t)\|A-B\|_{\mathrm{F}}^2 \le \|A+B\|_{\mathrm{F}}^2$ for every dimension $n\ge1$. In particular, Bourin's crossed-Heinz inequality $\|A^t B^{1-t}+B^t A^{1-t}\|_{\mathrm{F}} \le \|A+B\|_{\mathrm{F}}$ holds with equality if and only if $A=B$.

papers.title: Commutants of diagonal operators
papers.abstract: The aim of this paper is devoted to the profound and comprehensive characterization when diagonal operators having the minimal or double commutant property on a separable Hilbert space, in terms of the topological and geometric properties of their spectra.

papers.title: The random Riesz's lemma in random normed modules
papers.abstract: Riesz's lemma states that a normed space is finite-dimensional if and only if its closed unit ball is sequentially compact. The purpose of this paper is to establish a random counterpart of this lemma in a random normed module. Precisely speaking, based on the two recent developments in random functional analysis: one is the dimensional decomposition of a regular $\sigma$-stable $L^0$-module, and the other is the theory of random sequential compactness in a random normed module, we can finally establish the random Riesz's lemma, which states that a $\sigma$-stable random normed module is proper if and only if its random closed unit ball is random sequentially compact.

papers.title: $(\alpha,\beta)$-lineability and spaceability of functions with a unique maximum
papers.abstract: Motivated by the classical work of Gurariy and Quarta on linear spaces of continuous functions with a unique point of maximum, we determine the largest possible dimension of such spaces in several settings. For a connected $n$-manifold $M$ without boundary, with $n\ge2$, the largest dimension of a subspace of $\mathcal{C}_0(M)$ whose nonzero elements attain their maximum at exactly one point is $n+1$ if $M$ is homeomorphic to $S^n$, and $n$ otherwise. We also establish the sharp bound $n+1$ in $\mathcal{C}(\mathbb R^n)$ and obtain results on extensions of prescribed finite-dimensional subspaces.

papers.title: Hadamard inverse mapping theorem for certain continuously Gateaux differentiable mappings
papers.abstract: Hadamard inverse mapping theorem concerns global inversion of continuously differentiable mappings between Banach spaces. Here we consider a weaker notion of smoothness and work with continuously Gateaux differentiable mappings. We prove that a continuously Gateaux differentiable mapping with invertible derivatives such that the inverses are uniformly bounded, possesses a continuous right inverse on every compact set. We also provide sufficient conditions for global invertibility of certain continuously Gateaux differentiable mappings between Banach spaces.

papers.title: Generalized and Convex Poincar\'e Inequalities via Transport-Divergence Inequalities
papers.abstract: We investigate the relationship between generalized $(q',p')$-Poincar\'e inequalities and transport-divergence inequalities involving $\chi^q$-type divergences. Extending the classical correspondence between the $(2,2)$-Poincar\'e inequality and quadratic transport-$\chi^2$ inequalities, we prove that a $(q',p')$-Poincar\'e inequality is equivalent to a transport-divergence inequality for conjugates $(p,p')$ and $(q,q')$. We then study the convex counterpart of these inequalities. Using weak barycentric optimal transport and convex order, we establish an equivalence between convex $(q',p')$-Poincar\'e inequalities and weak transport-divergence inequalities involving a projected $\chi_q$ divergence. We further characterize the minimizers arising in this projection problem through a geometric condition on the relative density. In dimension one, we analyze the geometric consequences of $(q',p')$-Poincar\'e inequalities by identifying sharp conditions on the behavior of the density both at infinity and near isolated zeros. We show that when $q'>p'$, the concentration behavior becomes polynomial rather than exponential at infinity. Finally, we interpret these inequalities through the lens of optimization in Wasserstein space. In particular, the equivalence between transport-divergence and Poincar\'e inequalities appears as an analogue of the equivalence between quadratic growth and Polyak--\L ojasiewicz inequalities in finite-dimensional optimization.

papers.title: A Sharp Perimeter Inequality for Mean Distances on Convex Curves
papers.abstract: For a planar convex body $K$, let $\theta(K)$ denote the expected Euclidean distance between two independent points uniformly distributed on $\partial K$ with respect to arclength. We prove the sharp inequality $$\frac{\theta(K)}{\operatorname{per}K}>\frac{1}{6}.$$ The constant is approached by rectangles degenerating to a segment.

papers.title: Michelson and Logarithmic Operator Contrasts Spectral Geometry, Tracial Extensions, and Random Products
papers.abstract: The Michelson contrast of a positive invertible operator is a bounded coordinate for its condition number. Its logarithmic lift, $\operatorname{OLC}(A)=\frac12\log(\|A\|\|A^{-1}\|)$, connects spectral spread with projective Thompson geometry. This preprint collects the Novikov--Nikolaeva series and the associated single-author extensions by Novikov into one treatment. We develop the equality criterion for product subadditivity, its dimension and Jordan-rank thresholds, quantum-state examples, and contrasts associated with unitarily invariant norms. The latter have a sharp additive defect, while the full Schatten family records a logarithmic spectral profile up to homometry. Tracial extensions give characterisations of traces, dimension-sensitive defects, and spectral-edge asymptotics. Unbounded operators are described through critical exponents and finite sections. Tensor, matrix and free independence lead to distinct growth laws for products. Finally, symmetric cones provide a setting for the equality criterion, Lorentz boosts, and Jordan products. Classical ingredients are distinguished from the refinements developed in the series; conjectural asymptotic statements remain explicitly labelled.

papers.title: Actions of quantum groups: the standard implementation and relatively invariant weights
papers.abstract: We establish a characterisation of the standard implementation for actions of locally compact quantum groups on von Neumann algebras, extending results of Daws-Skalski-Viselter and Haagerup. As a consequence, we prove that taking the standard implementation respects morphisms of quantum groups. We also prove that several natural conditions expressing relative $\rho$-invariance for n.s.f. weights are equivalent.

papers.title: Adapted transport inequalities in continuous time
papers.abstract: Given a strong solution $X$ to a stochastic differential equation (SDE), we establish sufficient conditions under which $\text{Law}(X)$ satisfies an adapted quadratic transport cost inequality (AQTCI) with respect to the semimartingale adapted Wasserstein distance. When the drift and diffusion coefficients are Markovian, we further show that the AQTCI tensorizes in a dimension-free manner. As a corollary, we show that various stochastic control problems, e.g. optimal stopping and mean-variance portfolio selection, are stable under bounded, measurable drift perturbations. Additionally, we derive concentration inequalities (with respect to certain dynamic risk measures) for stochastic integrals $\int H_s dX_s$ and deduce appropriate bounds on their tail behavior. Furthermore, using the functional It\^o formula, we show that the AQTCI for $\text{Law}(X)$ allows one to deduce classical transport inequalities for $\text{Law}(F(X))$ even when $F$ is not Lipschitz on path space. Finally, we give sufficient conditions for $\text{Law}(X)$ to satisfy AQTCIs when $X$ is a solution to a scalar fractional SDE or stochastic Volterra equation.

papers.title: Continuous improved H\"{o}lder and reverse H\"{o}lder inequalities for Gaussian random vectors
papers.abstract: We establish continuous versions of the improved H\"{o}lder and reverse H\"{o}lder inequalities for correlated Gaussian random vectors, where a finite covariance matrix is replaced by a covariance operator acting on a Hilbert space of parameter fields. Under operator comparisons between the covariance and the exponent multiplier, we prove both inequalities and characterize equality in terms of a compatible probability density on the underlying Gaussian space. We further describe this density as a product of independent factors on common eigenspaces and a Gaussian factor whose mean and covariance satisfy explicit algebraic conditions. In the reverse setting, positive and negative exponents may coexist. The continuous product is defined by ordered truncation, allowing zeros in the positive-exponent factors. The equality proof combines an exact Ornstein--Uhlenbeck semigroup comparison, a spectral gap away from the kernel of the governing operator difference, and characteristic-function deconvolution. We also treat exponential quadratic functions without requiring a uniform positive-definiteness margin on the precision matrices.

papers.title: Sharp Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequalities
papers.abstract: We prove Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequalities for multiple sets. These are of the type: $$\prod_{i=1}^I \gamma_{\Sigma_i}(K_i)^{\tilde \lambda_i} \le C_{\text{sharp}}\gamma_\Gamma\Big(\sum_{i=1}^I \lambda_i K_i\Big),$$ with convex sets $K_i \subset \mathbb{R}^n$, whose barycenter $b_{K_i,\Sigma_i}$ with respect to the Gaussian measure $\gamma_{\Sigma_i}$ is zero, where $\lambda_i, \tilde \lambda_i \in (0;1)$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^I \lambda_i=\sum_{i=1}^I \tilde \lambda_i=1.$ In addition, we provide natural conditions on the matrices $\Gamma, \Sigma_1,\cdots,\Sigma_I \in \mathrm{Sym}_{>0}(n)$, which are given through a pointwise inequality involving the Karcher mean. Furthermore, we study equality cases of the corresponding functional forms in such situations. We also investigate the role of centering in the (B)-property by giving a counterexample for convex bodies with zero Lebesgue barycenters in dimensions at least three and thereby answering negatively a question of Faifman-Polterovich in \cite{Faifman_Polt}. Finally, a new slicing approach is introduced, which allows us to pass from centered convex sets to sets with arbitrary barycenters such that their weighted sum is convex. Based on this idea, we show a new Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequality $$e^{|\sum_{i=1}^I \lambda_i b_{K_i,I_n}|^2/2n} \gamma_n \Big(\sum_{i=1}^I \lambda_i K_i \Big)^{1/n} \ge \sum_{i=1}^I \lambda_i e^{|b_{K_i,I_n}|^2/2n} \gamma_n(K_i)^{1/n},$$ and consider a further application in the direction of the Gaussian correlation inequality, together with the rigidity for both inequalities.

papers.title: The Bessis Moussa Villani conjecture in finite von Neumann algebras
papers.abstract: We prove the Bessis--Moussa--Villani conjecture, which is known for matrix algebras, for bounded operators in a finite von Neumann algebra with a faithful normal tracial state. Following the approach of Heinavaara, for a pair of positive operators, we construct a tracial joint spectral measure on the punctured plane whose moments are the traces of symmetrized words. We construct a scalar measure by holomorphic spectral selection and a Lyapunov identity. An integral identity for its moments then gives positivity of two coordinate-weighted distributions. From these we obtain the planar measure and the Laplace representation of the trace exponential.

papers.title: Boundary Feller-Dynkin processes associated with Laguerre processes and Pickrell diffusions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we construct a Feller-Dynkin boundary process by applying the method of intertwiners to the coherent family, introduced in our previous work, of Laguerre processes with a fixed parameter. The corresponding boundary process is computed explicitly, and it turns out to be a deterministic dynamical system. Since the Pickrell diffusions that leave the Pickrell measure invariant are coherent with respect to the same projective system, we also obtain the stochastic boundary process associated with the coherent family of Pickrell diffusions.

papers.title: On the Fourier Mean Bodies of a Convex Body
papers.abstract: In 1998, R. Gardner and G. Zhang introduced the radial $p$th mean bodies $R_pK$ of a convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$, $p>-1$, which have since become important objects in geometric tomography. In this paper, we study the Fourier transforms of the radial functions of $R_pK$. This leads to a new family of star-shaped sets $F_pK$, which we call the Fourier $p$th mean bodies of $K$. We prove Fourier inversion formulas connecting $R_pK$ and $F_pK$, realizing them as $p$-intersection bodies in the sense of A. Koldobsky. We develop the basic affine geometry of $F_pK$; this includes affine covariance and monotonicity properties. We give sufficient conditions for the compactness of $F_pK$ in terms of the decay of $|\widehat{\chi_K}|^2$. We show that $F_pK$ is an origin-symmetric convex body for every $0<p\le1$. This range is sharp in general: already for the cube, $F_p[-1,1]^n$ is not convex for $1<p<2$ and $n\geq 2,$ while $F_p[-1,1]^n$ is not compact for $p\geq 2$. We further investigate the features Fourier mean bodies share with intersection bodies: we prove Hensley-type estimates for $F_pK$ when $K$ is isotropic and investigate an affine isoperimetric inequality.

papers.title: The Operator Systems of Hankel Matrices and Complex Polynomials
papers.abstract: Using polynomial matrix spectral factorization, we establish a complete order duality between $(n+1)\times(n+1)$ Hankel matrices and complex polynomials of degree at most $2n$ on the real line. The projection construction and trace pairing identify $e_n(t)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}t^{2j}$ as the polynomial order unit corresponding to the restriction of the matrix trace. The Cayley transform relates these matrix orders to Toeplitz matrices and truncated trigonometric polynomials, but for $n\geq 2$ the polynomial systems with units $e_n$ and $(1+t^2)^n$ are not unital order isomorphic. We establish polynomial minimality and Hankel maximality, and characterize positivity of $C^*$-algebra-valued block Hankel matrices through completely positive maps on the polynomial operator system. An augmented Vandermonde decomposition describes polynomial states as trace-one positive Hankel matrices, with extreme states given by normalized evaluations and the leading-coefficient functional at infinity.

papers.title: The dimension-free threshold for maximal sections of $\ell_p$
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of a sharp threshold $p_0 \approx 26.265\ldots$, such that for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and $p\geq p_0$, the volume maximizing section of the unit ball of $\ell_p^n$ is the section with Ball's hyperplane $(\frac{e_1+e_2}{\sqrt{2}})^\perp$, whereas for $p\in(2,p_0)$ the asymptotic maximizer as the ambient dimension $n\to\infty$ is the hyperplane orthogonal to the diagonal vector $\frac{e_1+\cdots+e_n}{\sqrt{n}}$.

papers.title: Auxiliary Gradient-Flow Solvers for Generalized Newtonian Models
papers.abstract: We introduce an auxiliary gradient-flow framework for variational problems with generalized Newtonian structure governed by an N-function. The key idea is to replace the nonlinear constitutive dependence on the gradient, or symmetric gradient, by an auxiliary scalar variable representing its squared magnitude. This shifts the nonlinearity from the state equation to the auxiliary variable, yielding a sequence of uniformly elliptic weighted linear problems. At the continuous level, we construct an auxiliary energy on a metric space adapted to the growth of the underlying N-function. In this topology, we prove lower semicontinuity, geodesic $\lambda$-convexity, and exponential convergence of the associated minimizing-movement scheme. At the finite element level, we derive a metric gradient flow through an explicit Riesz map, prove global well-posedness of the resulting semi-discrete ODE, and establish convergence to the finite element solution of the Euler--Lagrange equations of the generalized Newtonian energy. For the $p$-Laplacian and $p$-Stokes models, this gives a rigorous convergence result for $4/3\le p\le 4$, $p\ne2$, with asymptotic rate estimates beyond this range. We also propose practical time discretizations, including an operator-splitting scheme that gives the \kac iteration as a special case, and an adaptive pseudo-transient method that can be implemented using scalable linear solvers. Numerical experiments for power-law, Carreau--Yasuda, regularized Bingham, and optimal-design models demonstrate robustness, mesh-independent iteration counts in the tested regimes, and performance that matches or outperforms Newton's method.

papers.title: Regularized Brascamp-Lieb inequalities via Optimal Transport and Study of Equality Cases
papers.abstract: We consider regularized Brascamp-Lieb inequalities using the theory of optimal transportation, more precisely an anisotropic version of Caffarelli's contraction theorem. Furthermore, we provide a full picture concerning the issues of finiteness of the Brascamp-Lieb constant and of the existence of Gaussian extremizers, and completely determine all optimizers. The characterization of equality cases requires several new ideas to deal with difficulties, which do not appear for the non-regularized Brascamp-Lieb datum. Finally, we give applications retrieving Brascamp-Lieb-type inequalities with respect to the Gaussian measure and a regularized hypercontractivity inequality.

papers.title: A Classification Theorem on Non-compact Embeddings between Besov Spaces
papers.abstract: We analyze the embedding properties between Besov spaces, defined on the total space $\mathbb R^n$ and on bounded domains. We give a complete classification on whether or not these embedding maps satisfy certain weaker forms of compactness characterized by the so-called strictly and finitely strictly singular conditions. The result extends the recent findings on Sobolev embeddings by offering a refined description of the quality of non-compactness in the setting of Besov spaces.

papers.title: A Bourgain-Gromov problem on non-compact Sobolev-Lorentz embeddings
papers.abstract: We study the non-compact Sobolev embeddings into the optimal scale of Lorentz spaces, $W_0^mL^{p,q}(\Omega) \to L^{\frac{dp}{d - mp},r}(\Omega)$, where $\Omega \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$, $1 \leq m < d$, $0<q<r\le\infty$ with $1<p<\frac dm$ or $p=q=1$. We show that these embeddings are finitely strictly singular with certain upper bounds on the decay rate of the Bernstein numbers. We reduce the Sobolev embeddings to embeddings of Besov spaces and sequence spaces, which simplifies the previous methods by Bourgain-Gromov and Lang-Mihula.

papers.title: Annihilating ideals and Agler--McCarthy spectral varieties in the bidisc
papers.abstract: The closed unit bidisc $\overline{\mathbb{D}^2}$ is known to be a spectral set for any pair $(T_1,T_2)$ of commuting contractions. When each $T_i$ is pure and has finite defect, the pair admits a much smaller spectral set: the closure of a distinguished variety $V\subset \mathbb{D}^2$. We exhibit conditions on $(T_1,T_2)$ that guarantee that no proper closed subset of $\overline{V}$ can be a spectral set. In addition, we examine the relationship between $V$ and the annihilating ideal $Ann(T_1,T_2)$ in $H^\infty(\mathbb{D}^2)$. While $V$ is typically strictly larger than the zero set of $Ann(T_1,T_2)$, we isolate a natural constrained co-extension $(S_1,S_2)$ of $(T_1,T_2)$ whose Taylor spectrum is contained in $V$ and is closely linked to the so-called support of $Ann(T_1,T_2)$. We also find simple conditions on $Ann(T_1)$ detecting whether $Ann(T_1,T_2)$ is the ideal of functions vanishing on the joint point spectrum of $(S_1^*,S_2^*)$.
